name: ALGANT consortium
header:
ALGANT consortium
Europe / Canada · Two-year international master’s in Algebra, Geometry and Number Theory
Relevant European programme; no numerical ranking asserted
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• January 24, 2027 is explicitly posted, but the cohort heading is stale/inconsistent.
• Do not merge the ALGANT referee checklist with the ordinary Leiden MSc checklist.
• Funding may determine the allowed mobility pathway.
• Historical consortium doctorate is not a current advertised BA-to-PhD route.

sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Mathematics bachelor or equivalent of at least three years, with strong algebra/geometry/number-theory
preparation. UChicago BA is potentially eligible; selection is academic. Final-year students may apply
conditionally, finishing before the next academic year. Already having a master’s is not disqualifying. [apply]
[faq]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Apply through apply.algant.eu; choose a preferred two-country mobility pathway and indicate flexibility. The
consortium has Bordeaux, Concordia, Duisburg-Essen, Leiden, Milano, Padova, Paris-Saclay and Regensburg.
Admission later requires visas, permits and insurance. [home] [apply]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
Master’s selection does not publicly require prior supervisor agreement. Potential advisers depend on the
mobility path: see the Leiden and Paris-Saclay faculty dossiers. The current consortium is a master’s route; its
historical PhD programme operated 2009-2014 and is not advertised as a current direct PhD. [home] [apply]
Portal workflow [Unresolved]
Public instructions link to apply.algant.eu for registration, form and uploads. No account was created; referee
mechanics, document receipt indicators and replacement controls remain unverified. [apply]
Cycle verification [Conflict]
Current homepage has explicit application dates ending January 24, 2027 but an inconsistent 2026-2028
cohort label. Treat the dates as posted and confirm intake with the consortium. [home]

sections.title: Deadlines by stage
sections.text:
Academic application [Conflict]
Homepage explicitly says November 1, 2026 to January 24, 2027. No hour/time zone published. Its heading
simultaneously says cohort 2026-2028, inconsistent with those dates; confirm intended September 2027
intake. Generic apply page says mid-November opening. [home] [apply]
Funding consideration [Conflict]
Scholarship selection is integrated with the consortium application, whose current posted close is January 24,
2027. No separate later funding deadline found. Cohort-label conflict must be clarified. [home] [apply]

Reference receipt [Unresolved]
At least two academic referees are contacted by the consortium. No separate referee deadline or grace period
published; obtain the portal instruction and do not assume letters may arrive after January 24. [apply]
Test-score receipt [Unresolved]
No distinct English-evidence deadline published; include qualifying evidence with the application and check
both host universities. [apply] [faq]
Supporting documents [Standing rule]
Upload supporting documents in the consortium application; separate later host-enrolment requirements follow
selection. No public late-document grace established. Generic timeline has host enrolment May-July. [apply]
Accepting an offer [Unresolved]
Individual offer response deadline not public. Results generally March/April and at least four months before
courses; first host enrolment generally May-July. [apply]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Standing rule]
Strong written/spoken English; consortium accepts recognised test evidence or proof of English-taught
bachelor, subject to its decision. Host-specific rules still apply. FAQ sends Leiden applicants to current
university rules; Padova specifies B2. Concordia has separate official minimums which should be checked
directly for the chosen pathway. [apply] [faq]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
A UChicago English-taught BA is relevant evidence, but the consortium FAQ expressly makes exemptions
discretionary. Obtain consortium and both hosts’ acceptance; do not treat the Leiden US-degree exemption as
automatically binding every partner. [faq]
GRE General; GRE Mathematics [Unresolved]
No GRE requirement or consideration policy found in consortium instructions/FAQ; not established whether
unsolicited scores can be uploaded. [apply] [faq]

sections.title: Academic records
sections.text:
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
Scans of records from every higher-education institution attended, and highest degree evidence with credits,
grades and workload. Translations into English, French, German, Italian or Dutch accepted. Final-year
completion can be conditional. [apply]
Mathematics-course list [Standing rule]
Academic records include courses. A separate mathematical-course-list template is not specified publicly.
[apply]
Course descriptions [Unresolved]
Separate course descriptions are not specified in the public consortium checklist; a host may request them.
Format/limit unverified. [apply]

Detailed CV required, uploaded. No public length or formatting limit. [apply]
Statement of purpose [Standing rule]

generally. No public length/font/margin limit. [apply]
Personal / background statement [Unresolved]

supplementary question remains unverified. [apply]
Research-interest statement [Unresolved]
No separate research-interest essay listed; motivation can address mathematical interests. Independent
prompt/limit unverified. [apply]
Research proposal [Unresolved]

independent proposal established. [apply]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Standing rule]
No universal stipend: merit-based individual scholarship offers and partial/full fee waivers. Amount, gross/net
status, payment months, insurance and travel support must be read in the actual offer. [faq]
Years of support [Unresolved]
Master’s lasts two years, typically at two partner universities in different countries. Award duration/renewal
conditions are individual and not publicly quantified. [home] [faq]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
FAQ makes mathematics bachelor/equivalent applicants eligible for merit scholarship consideration without a
stated nationality restriction. Visa and host admission requirements still apply. [faq] [apply]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Some scholarships constrain the mobility pathway. Academic merit drives allocation; the public FAQ provides
no universal progress threshold or guaranteed second-year amount. [faq]
Extra funding application [Unresolved]
The consortium application is used for selection and scholarships/fee waivers. Any funding-selection checkbox
or separate portal declaration is not publicly described. [apply] [faq]
Other funding routes [Unresolved]
Host-country/host-university awards may have their own eligibility and combination rules. No additional award
is guaranteed by ALGANT; consult Leiden/Paris-Saclay and chosen hosts separately. [home] [faq]
Application fee [Unresolved]
Nominal programme tuition €4,000/year; merit fee waivers available. A separate consortium application fee is
not published, so do not equate absence of a listed fee with a confirmed €0 charge. [faq]
Fee waiver [Unresolved]
Programme fee-waiver decisions are merit-based. Application-fee-waiver logistics are not published because
no application charge was established. [faq]

ALGANT consortium
Europe / Canada · Two-year international master’s in Algebra, Geometry and Number Theory
Relevant European programme; no numerical ranking asserted
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• January 24, 2027 is explicitly posted, but the cohort heading is stale/inconsistent.
• Do not merge the ALGANT referee checklist with the ordinary Leiden MSc checklist.
• Funding may determine the allowed mobility pathway.
• Historical consortium doctorate is not a current advertised BA-to-PhD route.
Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Mathematics bachelor or equivalent of at least three years, with strong algebra/geometry/number-theory
preparation. UChicago BA is potentially eligible; selection is academic. Final-year students may apply
conditionally, finishing before the next academic year. Already having a master’s is not disqualifying. [apply]
[faq]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Apply through apply.algant.eu; choose a preferred two-country mobility pathway and indicate flexibility. The
consortium has Bordeaux, Concordia, Duisburg-Essen, Leiden, Milano, Padova, Paris-Saclay and Regensburg.
Admission later requires visas, permits and insurance. [home] [apply]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
Master’s selection does not publicly require prior supervisor agreement. Potential advisers depend on the
mobility path: see the Leiden and Paris-Saclay faculty dossiers. The current consortium is a master’s route; its
historical PhD programme operated 2009-2014 and is not advertised as a current direct PhD. [home] [apply]
Portal workflow [Unresolved]
Public instructions link to apply.algant.eu for registration, form and uploads. No account was created; referee
mechanics, document receipt indicators and replacement controls remain unverified. [apply]
Cycle verification [Conflict]
Current homepage has explicit application dates ending January 24, 2027 but an inconsistent 2026-2028
cohort label. Treat the dates as posted and confirm intake with the consortium. [home]
Deadlines by stage
Academic application [Conflict]
Homepage explicitly says November 1, 2026 to January 24, 2027. No hour/time zone published. Its heading
simultaneously says cohort 2026-2028, inconsistent with those dates; confirm intended September 2027
intake. Generic apply page says mid-November opening. [home] [apply]
Funding consideration [Conflict]
Scholarship selection is integrated with the consortium application, whose current posted close is January 24,
2027. No separate later funding deadline found. Cohort-label conflict must be clarified. [home] [apply]

Reference receipt [Unresolved]
At least two academic referees are contacted by the consortium. No separate referee deadline or grace period
published; obtain the portal instruction and do not assume letters may arrive after January 24. [apply]
Test-score receipt [Unresolved]
No distinct English-evidence deadline published; include qualifying evidence with the application and check
both host universities. [apply] [faq]
Supporting documents [Standing rule]
Upload supporting documents in the consortium application; separate later host-enrolment requirements follow
selection. No public late-document grace established. Generic timeline has host enrolment May-July. [apply]
Accepting an offer [Unresolved]
Individual offer response deadline not public. Results generally March/April and at least four months before
courses; first host enrolment generally May-July. [apply]
English and GRE
English requirement [Standing rule]
Strong written/spoken English; consortium accepts recognised test evidence or proof of English-taught
bachelor, subject to its decision. Host-specific rules still apply. FAQ sends Leiden applicants to current
university rules; Padova specifies B2. Concordia has separate official minimums which should be checked
directly for the chosen pathway. [apply] [faq]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
A UChicago English-taught BA is relevant evidence, but the consortium FAQ expressly makes exemptions
discretionary. Obtain consortium and both hosts’ acceptance; do not treat the Leiden US-degree exemption as
automatically binding every partner. [faq]
GRE General; GRE Mathematics [Unresolved]
No GRE requirement or consideration policy found in consortium instructions/FAQ; not established whether
unsolicited scores can be uploaded. [apply] [faq]
Academic records
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
Scans of records from every higher-education institution attended, and highest degree evidence with credits,
grades and workload. Translations into English, French, German, Italian or Dutch accepted. Final-year
completion can be conditional. [apply]
Mathematics-course list [Standing rule]
Academic records include courses. A separate mathematical-course-list template is not specified publicly.
[apply]
Course descriptions [Unresolved]
Separate course descriptions are not specified in the public consortium checklist; a host may request them.
Format/limit unverified. [apply]
Recommendation letters
Number and type [Standing rule]
At least two academic staff referees, identified by email address in the application. [apply]
Scholarship references [Unresolved]
Recommendations are part of the integrated scholarship selection. No extra scholarship-only referee or distinct
questionnaire published. [apply]

What sends the invitation [Unresolved]
Consortium says it contacts named academics. It does not say whether email is triggered by saving details,
validation, or final submission. [apply]
Before versus after submission [Unresolved]
No public evidence that submission is required before invitations; verify in the portal before alerting referees to
the expected timing. [apply]
Receipt confirmation [Unresolved]
Reference-specific receipt display is not publicly documented; portal access was not used to create an
application. [apply]
Updating and reusing letters [Unresolved]
Letter replacement, update and reuse rules are not publicly documented. [apply]
Written materials
Academic CV / resume [Standing rule]
Detailed CV required, uploaded. No public length or formatting limit. [apply]
Statement of purpose [Standing rule]
Motivation letter required, uploaded. Faithful paraphrase: explain your interest in ALGANT and in mathematics
generally. No public length/font/margin limit. [apply]
Personal / background statement [Unresolved]
No separately identified background statement; the motivation letter is the named narrative. Any portal-only
supplementary question remains unverified. [apply]
Research-interest statement [Unresolved]
No separate research-interest essay listed; motivation can address mathematical interests. Independent
prompt/limit unverified. [apply]
Research proposal [Unresolved]
No research proposal listed for this taught/research master’s. No optional-upload permission for an
independent proposal established. [apply]
Writing sample / thesis / research summary [Standing rule]
Other credential evidence, including research memoirs or competition diplomas, may accompany the
application. Upload is the stated mechanism; link-only substitution, file limits and length limits unverified.
[apply]
Publications list [Unresolved]
No distinct publications-list instruction; a detailed CV is required. Separate paper upload/link rules not
specified. [apply]
Course-list document [Unresolved]
No separate written course-list format beyond academic records specified. [apply]
Scholarship essays [Unresolved]
No separate scholarship essay publicly specified beyond integrated motivation and application. Additional
portal short answers unverified. [apply]
Other short answers / materials [Unresolved]
Mobility preferences/flexibility are requested. Further form fields, exact character limits and formatting cannot
be verified from the public pages. [apply]

Funding and fees
Amount and coverage [Standing rule]
No universal stipend: merit-based individual scholarship offers and partial/full fee waivers. Amount, gross/net
status, payment months, insurance and travel support must be read in the actual offer. [faq]
Years of support [Unresolved]
Master’s lasts two years, typically at two partner universities in different countries. Award duration/renewal
conditions are individual and not publicly quantified. [home] [faq]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
FAQ makes mathematics bachelor/equivalent applicants eligible for merit scholarship consideration without a
stated nationality restriction. Visa and host admission requirements still apply. [faq] [apply]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Some scholarships constrain the mobility pathway. Academic merit drives allocation; the public FAQ provides
no universal progress threshold or guaranteed second-year amount. [faq]
Extra funding application [Unresolved]
The consortium application is used for selection and scholarships/fee waivers. Any funding-selection checkbox
or separate portal declaration is not publicly described. [apply] [faq]
Other funding routes [Unresolved]
Host-country/host-university awards may have their own eligibility and combination rules. No additional award
is guaranteed by ALGANT; consult Leiden/Paris-Saclay and chosen hosts separately. [home] [faq]
Application fee [Unresolved]
Nominal programme tuition €4,000/year; merit fee waivers available. A separate consortium application fee is
not published, so do not equate absence of a listed fee with a confirmed €0 charge. [faq]
Fee waiver [Unresolved]
Programme fee-waiver decisions are merit-based. Application-fee-waiver logistics are not published because
no application charge was established. [faq]
Conflicts and remaining checks
Conflicting sources [Conflict]
Homepage says opening November 1, 2026 and closing January 24, 2027 while labelling the master’s
2026-2028; generic instructions say opening mid-November. Host language policies may be newer than the
2023 FAQ and govern host admission. [home] [apply] [faq]
Checks still needed [Unresolved]
Confirm cohort year, exact closing time, referee deadline/trigger/receipt, UChicago language evidence for both
chosen hosts, all award amounts/payment periods and response deadlines. This consortium-level dossier is not
a full admissions dossier for each of the eight hosts; Leiden and Paris-Saclay are covered separately. [home]
[apply] [faq]
Potential advisers and recent research
No paper-verified adviser entry is present. Consult the adviser-contact and unresolved-actions fields for the
boundary of the research.
